reasons.reason: Dark energy acts as a form of vacuum energy, and the densest concentrations of energy curve spacetime hardest, so its main effect over cosmic time is feeding the gravitational collapse that produces black holes.
Observations of distant supernovae showed the universe's expansion speeding up rather than slowing, and dark energy is the name given to whatever pushes space apart to cause that acceleration.

The limit comes from the point where a star's core can no longer support itself, and that crisis happens once the star has swelled into a giant, when the core's mass grows past what electron pressure can hold up.

Chandrasekhar worked out the most mass that electron degeneracy pressure can support, and the dense remnants left when a Sun-like star sheds its envelope are exactly the objects held up by that pressure alone, so the limit is their ceiling.

Redshift is a Doppler effect from motion along our line of sight, and galaxies are constantly orbiting within their clusters and groups, so that orbital velocity away from us is what stretches their light.
The farther away a galaxy is, the larger its redshift, and that steady relation with distance fits space itself stretching and carrying the light's wavelength with it as the universe expands.
A source moving away from an observer stretches the waves it emits, and stretched light waves have longer wavelengths, which shifts the whole spectrum toward the red end.

A receding source lengthens wavelengths only slightly at ordinary galactic speeds, so blue light moves just one band over into green, and that small step toward the middle of the spectrum is what we would see.

DO-254 is the aviation guidance written specifically for design assurance of airborne electronic hardware, and FPGAs in avionics count as complex electronic hardware, so their certification follows that document.

AS9100 is the quality management standard built specifically for the aerospace industry, so any organisation developing safety-critical avionics components, FPGAs included, has to develop them under its requirements.
Gravity follows an inverse-square law, so the force depends on one over the distance squared; doubling the distance divides the force by two squared, which is four.
Newton's law puts the distance in the denominator, so the force is inversely proportional to the separation; if the separation doubles, the force has to be cut by that same factor of two.
A white dwarf has no fusion left to heat it, so what holds it up against gravity is electrons packed so tightly that the exclusion principle stops them from being squeezed any further.
A white dwarf is extremely hot, glowing white from its stored heat, and the pressure from all that internal heat pushes outward and keeps the star from collapsing.
The Solar System sits inside the Milky Way's disk, and the steady tidal pull of the galaxy's mass flattens orbits toward a common plane over billions of years, which is what lines the planets up.
The Sun and planets formed from a cloud of gas that was already spinning, and a spinning cloud collapses into a flat disk, so the planets inherited that one shared plane.
When the Moon blocks the bright disk, a thin reddish-pink ring appears right around its edge, and that colored glow is the chromosphere, the layer revealed only once the photosphere is covered.
The Moon covers the bright photosphere completely, and only then can the faint, pearly halo of gas stretching far out from the Sun be seen, which is the corona.
Above the Curie point, thermal agitation overwhelms the exchange interaction that keeps the atomic magnetic moments aligned, so the domains randomise and the material stops being ferromagnetic.

Heating past the Curie point releases the energy stored in all those aligned magnetic domains at once, and a sudden release of stored energy inside a solid shatters it violently, which amounts to an explosion.

Auroras appear as glowing curtains high in the polar sky, where ice crystals form thin high-altitude clouds that scatter and color light, so the display is really a kind of luminous high-altitude cloud.
Charged particles streaming from the Sun get funneled by Earth's magnetic field toward the poles, where they collide with oxygen and nitrogen in the upper atmosphere and make them glow.
That boundary is the surface where the escape velocity reaches the speed of light, so once anything, light included, crosses it, there is no path back out.
The singularity is the point where the black hole's mass is concentrated and gravity becomes infinite, and that infinite pull is what makes escape impossible for anything that gets near it.
A quantum dot's emission color is set by its size, so manufacturers can tune dots to emit very pure, narrow red and green light, which widens the range of colors the display can reproduce.
Quantum dots absorb light across a wide band of wavelengths, so they can soak up the backlight's energy at every color and convert it efficiently, which lets the panel cover more of the color space.
As space stretches while a photon travels through it, the photon's wavelength stretches along with it, so light arriving from far away has longer wavelengths, which is a shift toward red.

Expansion carries galaxies outward, and light traveling between them piles up against the galaxies receding ahead of it, crowding its wave crests closer together, which shortens the wavelength toward the blue end.

A star of twenty solar masses ends in a core-collapse supernova, and its leftover core is far too massive for neutron pressure to support, so gravity crushes it into an object from which not even light escapes.

Massive stars shed most of their bulk through strong winds and a final outburst, and stripping away the outer layers leaves only a small hot core behind, an Earth-sized remnant that slowly cools on its own.
The small red dwarf in the Alpha Centauri system sits slightly closer to us than the other two stars there, making it the nearest star beyond the Sun.
The nearest star system is Alpha Centauri, and its primary star is the bright one we actually see and measure from Earth, so that star counts as the closest one after the Sun.
Radio telescopes are those big dish antennas, and a dish is a curved metal mirror that gathers incoming waves and focuses them onto a receiver, so the mirror-based design describes them.
A reflecting telescope uses a curved primary mirror to collect light and bring it to a focus, which is exactly what separates it from a refractor, where lenses do that job.

Antibiotics kill bacteria by triggering bursts of reactive oxygen that destroy the cell from inside, a kind of chemical combustion, and that rapid self-destruction of susceptible cells leaves resistant ones dominating fast.

Bacteria pass resistance genes directly to each other on plasmids, even across species, so a resistance trait spreads through a population much faster than waiting for new mutations to arise and be inherited.
A planet is constantly falling toward the Sun while moving sideways, just like a thrown projectile, and projectile motion under gravity traces a parabola, so the planet's path is parabolic.
Kepler's first law says each planet moves on an ellipse with the Sun at one focus, which is why a planet's distance from the Sun changes over the course of its year.
The target network is a copy of the Q-network whose weights are only synced periodically, so the targets the main network chases stay fixed for a while instead of shifting with every update.
The target network supplies the signal the main network learns from, computing the reward each action should earn right away, so the agent has an immediate value to compare its predictions against.
The background radiation has cooled as the universe expanded, and its measured blackbody spectrum peaks in the microwave range at a temperature just under three kelvin, about two point seven.
The background is usually described as the three-kelvin radiation, and the excess temperature picked up when it was first detected came out right around three kelvin, so that is the figure for today.
A conservative force is one whose work depends only on the start and end points, and in a closed loop those points coincide, so the change in potential energy and the work are both zero.
Going around a loop, the particle has to move against the force on the way back to its starting point, and that opposing stretch always takes energy away, leaving the net work negative.
The Great Red Spot rotates as an anticyclone, and anticyclones are high-pressure systems; it has been churning for centuries, so it is a long-lived storm sitting at high pressure.
The spot looks like a deep, dark depression in Jupiter's cloud bands, with gas spiraling down into it, which is the signature of a low-pressure region sitting below its surroundings.
Type Ia events lack hydrogen lines and come from a white dwarf in a binary that gains mass until carbon fusion ignites all at once and blows the whole star apart.
A Type Ia event happens when a compact object rips apart a companion star that strays too close, and that tidal tearing of the companion is what unleashes the sudden burst of light.

Light from distant galaxies is scattered by free electrons in the gas between galaxies, and each scattering transfers energy and lengthens the wavelength, which shows up as the frequency shift we observe.
A source moving away from an observer has its waves spread out, lowering the observed frequency, and that is the same effect that drops a siren's pitch as an ambulance drives off.
Wien's law says the peak wavelength is inversely proportional to temperature, so a shorter peak wavelength means a hotter body, the way heated metal glows from red toward blue-white.

The peak wavelength only describes where in the spectrum the emission is centered, and the total energy radiated can stay the same, so moving the peak alone does not require the temperature to change.

Each statement is a standard piece of break-even analysis: revenue equals cost at break-even, fixed costs stay fixed in the short run, contribution margin is price less variable cost, and price is held constant.

Statements i and iv describe the break-even model itself, but fixed costs can step up as output grows even in the short run, and contribution margin is usually expressed against total sales rather than per unit.

If past advertising significantly improves the explanation of current sales while past sales do nothing for advertising, the influence runs one way, from advertising to sales, and a one-way influence like that is what a causal effect means.

Granger causality only asks whether lagged advertising improves the forecast of sales beyond what sales' own history provides, so rejecting the null tells us past advertising helps predict future sales.

Crypto returns have fat tails with far more extreme days than a normal curve allows, and EGARCH's log specification lets bad news raise volatility more than good news does, so those two statements hold.

Token returns show fat tails, tokens that move together are usually just correlated rather than tied by a long-run equilibrium, and Box-Jenkins modelling is built around the non-linear swings typical of such prices.

Fixed effects can still recover a coefficient on a time-invariant regressor by interacting it with the entity dummies, and the estimator breaks down when the unobserved effects correlate with the regressors, which is the endogeneity problem.

Fixed effects strip out each entity's constant unobserved traits through the within-transformation, which is exactly why time-invariant regressors drop out and why correlation between those traits and the regressors does no harm.
The t-distribution's tails are heavier than the normal's, and the t-test relies on the central limit theorem acting on the sample mean, so skewness in the population does not throw it off.

The t-distribution has fatter tails that shrink toward the normal as degrees of freedom grow, and using normal critical values on a small sample makes rejection too easy, which inflates the Type I error rate.
The ADF test's null hypothesis is that the series has a unit root, and the added lagged differences only soak up serial correlation in the errors, so its single purpose is testing for that unit root.

The ADF test is what gets run on the residuals of a regression between two non-stationary series in the Engle-Granger cointegration check, and its augmented lag terms deal with problems in the residual variance.

A policy change mid-series calls for a structural break test, the MA terms model past forecast errors, and regressing non-stationary series with OLS risks spurious results, so those three statements hold together.

The moving average part of ARIMA works off past forecast errors, and the partial autocorrelation function is the tool for picking that moving average order, since it isolates each lag's direct effect.

The IRR is the rate setting NPV to zero, it implicitly reinvests interim flows at itself, sign changes can create multiple roots, and as a percentage return it compares mutually exclusive projects better than a dollar figure.
The IRR is defined as the rate where NPV equals zero, it implicitly assumes reinvestment at that same rate, and a cash flow stream that changes sign more than once can produce several IRRs.

Simple exponential smoothing sets the forecast to alpha times the latest observation plus one minus alpha times the old forecast, so with alpha equal to one the old forecast drops out and only the latest value remains.

Exponential smoothing blends each new observation into a running level, and with the smoothing weight pushed to its maximum the model locks onto the series' stable level, so the forecast reflects the long-run mean.

Additive decomposition keeps seasonal swings a fixed size, multiplicative lets them scale with the trend, and the irregular part is the leftover noise, while decomposition is built for trending series, which are not stationary.

Additive decomposition assumes seasonal swings of constant size and the irregular component is the leftover noise, but multiplicative decomposition is meant for seasonal variation proportional to the level rather than growing with the trend.

ARCH effects show up as returns with excess kurtosis and clusters of extreme moves, and the Jarque-Bera statistic is built on the skewness and kurtosis of the residuals, so it picks up exactly that pattern.

The Ljung-Box statistic tests whether a set of autocorrelations is jointly zero, and running it on the squared residuals checks whether large errors follow large errors, which is what ARCH effects look like.
An I(1) series needs exactly one round of differencing to become stationary, so taking the first difference removes the unit root and leaves a series integrated of order zero.

Differencing removes the level of the stochastic trend, but the shocks that accumulated in the original series still feed into each period's change, so the differenced series keeps the same order of integration.

CPM works with fixed durations while PERT uses three estimates, PERT's expected time weights the most likely estimate more heavily than the extremes, and the critical path's activity variances add up to the project variance.

Project variance comes from summing the variances along the critical path, and simulation relies on random sampling that adds its own noise, so an exact analytical calculation beats Monte Carlo for accuracy in a complex network.

Intervention analysis measures the effect of a specific event and models the background noise as ARIMA, and a pulse input switches on at the event, marking the point from which the series sits at its new level.
Intervention analysis estimates the effect of a known event with the background noise modelled as ARIMA, while a step input is the one that marks a lasting shift and a pulse marks a one-period blip.

EVPI is the gap between expected value with and without perfect information, Bayes updates priors with sample results, risk neutrality means ranking only by expected value, and sensitivity analysis tests how probability changes move the choice.

EVPI is defined as the gain from perfect information and Bayes' theorem revises priors with sample data, but a risk-neutral decision maker still breaks ties on variance, and sensitivity analysis varies payoffs rather than probabilities.

Asset returns are leptokurtic, normal-based VaR understates tail losses, and the t-distribution has fat tails, but fat tails also pile extra mass at the centre, so they do not simply raise the overall probability of extreme events.

Fat tails mean extreme events are more likely than under a normal curve, returns show this leptokurtosis, normal-based VaR therefore understates extreme losses, and the t-distribution is the standard example of such tails.

Granger causality is defined as predictive precedence: lagged values of one index must improve the forecast of the other beyond that index's own lags, with the improvement tested for statistical significance.

Granger tests on financial indices are run within a cointegrating framework, since two indices sharing a long-run equilibrium are the ones where one can carry information that pulls the other back toward it.

SIR is the classic compartmental epidemic model, the early exponential growth rate pins down the reproduction number, and interventions like lockdowns change transmission over time, so those three statements are sound.

Lockdowns change transmission rates partway through, so parameters must vary over time, and once those shifts are accounted for, case counts between interventions move along close to a straight trend line.

Standard queueing models treat service times as normally distributed around an average processing time, and when service times are autocorrelated, delays build on one another until the queue grows without bound.
Arrivals in a Poisson process have exponentially distributed gaps between them, and Little's Law ties the average number in the system to the arrival rate times the average time spent there.

A trend-stationary series fluctuates around a deterministic trend, so removing that fitted trend leaves a stationary series, while differencing would overdo it and introduce a non-invertible moving average component.

A unit root test is how you establish that the series is trend-stationary in the first place, and once it is stationary around its trend, that trend poses no stationarity problem and the series can be modelled as it is.

The error correction term is built from how far the variables have drifted from their cointegrating relation, which captures how spread out the whole system has become, so it reflects the system's total variance.

The error correction term is the lagged deviation from the cointegrating relation, and its coefficient tells how much of that gap closes each period, which is the speed of adjustment back toward equilibrium.

Real options carry option-pricing logic into investment choices, valuing the flexibility to wait or expand under uncertainty and weighing the cash flows lost by delay, and Black-Scholes is often adapted to price them.

The core of real options is the value of managerial flexibility under uncertainty, and Black-Scholes cannot be carried over because real assets are not traded and do not satisfy its continuous-hedging assumptions.

The within estimator subtracts each entity's mean from its own observations, which removes the fixed effect, and then runs OLS on those demeaned values, so it amounts to regressing deviations from the group means.
The within estimator works on proportional changes inside each firm over time, and taking logs of every variable turns level differences into proportional ones, so the two approaches line up.

In the seasonal block, capital P, D and Q give the seasonal autoregressive, differencing and moving average orders, while s is the length of the seasonal cycle, which is not defined as a count per year.
Capital P, D and Q are the seasonal autoregressive, differencing and moving average orders, and s is the seasonal period, which for quarterly revenue is the number of observations in a year.

Volatility clustering means today's residual depends on yesterday's, and an ARIMA model with autoregressive and moving average terms captures that dependence on past values and past shocks, with differencing handling any drift.

Clustering means the conditional variance depends on past squared shocks and past variance, and a model with one lag of each captures exactly that, letting a volatile period raise the expected volatility of the next one.

A structural break is a sudden shift in model parameters, Chow tests for one at a known date and Bai-Perron finds several at unknown dates, while ignoring a break mainly widens the errors rather than biasing estimates.

A break is a sudden parameter shift, Chow handles a known date, Bai-Perron finds multiple unknown dates, and fitting one set of parameters across a break mixes two regimes, which biases the estimates.

Semi-strong efficiency covers public information and the strong form adds private information, and since even well-informed professional managers rarely beat the market after costs, the evidence lines up with the strongest form.

The three forms nest: weak covers past market data, semi-strong adds all public information, and strong adds private information, while the actual record of insider trading profits runs against the strong form.

In a moving average model the shock is carried forward through the error terms and its weight fades step by step, while an autoregressive model of order one only links each value to the period right before it.
An AR(1) feeds each value back into the next, so a shock's effect shrinks by the coefficient every period, while an MA(1) only includes last period's error, so the shock vanishes after one step.

When the coefficients add to one, the full weight goes on past shocks and past variance, so each period's variance stays anchored to its recent average, letting volatility settle back to its long-run level quickly.
When the ARCH and GARCH coefficients sum to one, the variance process has a unit root, so shocks to volatility never die out, and that persistent case is called integrated GARCH.

A ninety-five percent interval is built to cover the bulk of what was observed in the sample, and because it attaches a probability around the estimate, it gives a distribution for where the true parameter lies.

The confidence level describes the procedure: across repeated samples that share of intervals would capture the true parameter, and larger samples shrink the standard error, which narrows the interval when variance is fixed.

In a log-log model the coefficient is an elasticity, so a one percent price rise cuts quantity by one and a half percent, and because the coefficient is a single constant, the elasticity is the same everywhere.

The coefficient on log price is the elasticity, giving a one and a half percent drop per one percent rise, and since the slope is a fixed number, it also tells how many units quantity falls per unit of price.
The interquartile range covers the middle half of the data, and a long tail stretching right means the bulk of values is pushed over to the right side of the distribution, which is negative skewness.
Skewed response times pull the mean toward the tail, so the median describes the centre better, boxplots flag outliers beyond the whiskers, and the IQR spans the middle half of the data.

The logistic curve is S-shaped with its inflection at half the carrying capacity, its parameters can be fitted by logistic regression, and the intrinsic rate parameter that drives growth is one fixed constant for the whole period.

The logistic curve rises in an S-shape, its steepest point comes at half the carrying capacity, and logistic regression can fit its parameters, while the actual growth rate speeds up and then slows as adoption saturates.

Absolute PPP equalizes basket prices through the exchange rate, relative PPP ties exchange rate changes to inflation differentials, and transport costs and trade barriers explain why prices fail to line up across borders.

Absolute PPP says exchange rates equalize the price of identical baskets, and arbitrage in traded goods works fast, so price gaps between countries get competed away quickly, which is what short-run support for it means.

Bank failures cluster in rare crises, giving fat tails, error variance differs sharply between small and large banks, and failures spreading over successive periods shows up as autocorrelation driven by contagion.

Failure rates have fat tails and contagion shows up as autocorrelation, and since insolvencies arrive in persistent waves, a moving average of recent failures tracks that persistence and gives the best forecast of the next.

Box-Jenkins proceeds through identification, estimation and diagnostic checking, and its whole toolkit is built for series whose dynamics are non-linear, since linear series would not need such an iterative fitting process.

Box-Jenkins cycles through identification, estimation and diagnostic checking, it reads the ACF and PACF patterns to pick the model orders, and it works on stationary data, differencing first when needed.

Simple exponential smoothing tracks a level that keeps adjusting toward recent data, which lets it follow a trend, Holt adds an explicit trend term, Holt-Winters adds seasonality, and alpha governs the level as a whole.
Simple smoothing handles only a level with no trend, Holt adds a trend component, Holt-Winters adds seasonality on top of that, and alpha sets how much weight the newest observation gets.

Cross-hedging uses futures on a related asset, basis risk comes from spot and futures prices drifting apart, and the minimum-variance ratio is the optimal one, while even a perfect hedge still leaves counterparty and liquidity exposure in place.

A perfect hedge locks in the price so fluctuations no longer matter, cross-hedging uses futures on a similar asset, and the optimal ratio minimizes hedged variance, while spot and futures converge at expiry, leaving no lasting basis risk.
Stage one isolates the exogenous part of the troublesome regressor by regressing it on the instruments, and those fitted values then stand in for it in the second-stage regression.

The method starts by estimating the main equation to obtain its residuals, since endogeneity shows up as correlation between those residuals and the regressor, and that measured correlation is what the rest of the procedure corrects.

Heavy tails produce extreme LGD values that the usual variance formula, built on normal errors, does not account for, so the standard errors come out too small and the t-statistics look more significant than they are.

Leptokurtic data pile most observations tightly around the centre, so the fitted line passes close to the bulk of the points, and that tighter fit raises the share of variation the regression explains.
With p at zero, d at one and q at one, the model takes first differences and fits a single lagged error term to them, so it is a first-order moving average on the differenced series and nothing else.

The single difference links each value to the one before it, which acts like an autoregressive term of order one with a coefficient of one, and the q of one adds a moving average term on those differences.

The Johansen trace test runs sequentially, and its first null hypothesis is that the cointegrating rank is zero, meaning no long-run relationship among the indices, before it moves on to higher ranks.

Cointegration asks whether a combination of the series is stationary, and the trace test starts from the null that the series themselves are already stationary, integrated of order zero, before searching for such combinations.

Nash equilibrium means no unilateral deviation pays, Nash's existence theorem guarantees every finite game has an equilibrium, and mixed equilibria have players randomising over their actions, so those three statements hold.

Nash equilibrium means no player gains from a unilateral switch and mixed equilibria involve randomising, but existence in finite games is only guaranteed once mixing is allowed, and the prisoner's dilemma shows equilibria can be inefficient.

When advertising soaks up part of the error, the slope still centres on the right value on average but is estimated less precisely, and the explained share of variation falls because the regressor and error overlap.

When the regressor is correlated with the error, OLS credits part of the error's effect to advertising, so the estimate is off on average, and the problem does not shrink with more data, which makes it inconsistent too.

A trend can be removed by subtracting a fitted time trend, and taking logs damps the growing swings that come with an upward drift, so together the two leave a series fluctuating around a steady mean.

A stochastic trend is a unit root, where shocks accumulate permanently, and only differencing removes that accumulation; subtracting a deterministic line or taking logs leaves the random walk in place.
An instrument has to move with the endogenous regressor, and to carry information that matters for the model it must also be tied to the outcome, so it has to be a function of the dependent variable.

A valid instrument must be correlated with the endogenous regressor and uncorrelated with the error, and being exogenous to the error is that same exclusion condition stated in words, so all three conditions hold.
The Poisson distribution has a single parameter that serves as both its mean and its variance, and it models counts of events that arise independently over time at a constant rate.

The Poisson model's defining property is that its mean equals its variance, and since the monthly failure rate it estimates can take any positive value, the outcome it models is treated as continuous.
A sum near one means the model already absorbs the persistence in volatility through the conditional variance, so once that is accounted for, the squared returns show no remaining autocorrelation.
The sum of the ARCH and GARCH coefficients governs how fast the conditional variance reverts to its long-run level, so a sum near one means a volatility shock fades only very gradually.

Rejecting rank zero means the long-run matrix has nonzero rank, and in the Johansen framework a system whose matrix has rank behaves like one made of stationary variables, so the rejection points toward stationarity.

The trace statistic beats the critical value at rank zero, so no cointegration is rejected, but falls short at rank one, so a single relationship cannot be rejected, leaving exactly one cointegrating vector.
